question: Does accuracy depend on HOW MANY completion tokens carry gradient, independently of WHICH ones? A uniform random mask at each rate isolates the budget.
design: lr 1e-5 constant, 120 steps, 32 rollouts/step, DAPO-Math-17K (en); eval MATH500, 500 problems x 4 samples, greedy-free sampling seed 0. The random mask is redrawn uniformly over each batch's completion tokens every step.
finding: Two axes, measured separately at lr 1e-5 on MATH500. BUDGET (how many completion tokens receive gradient), swept with a uniform random mask from 0.20 to 1.00: total span 0.0143 against a seed SD of ~0.008, non-monotone, no cell significantly below full-token OPD. The budget does not matter anywhere in that 5x range. SELECTION (which tokens), measured against a uniform draw at the same budget: math_only +0.0243 (p=0.052), text_only -0.0148 (p=0.345). Selection is the only axis in this experiment that moves accuracy, and it moves it opposite to gradient-mass coverage -- the lower-divergence selection beats random, the higher-divergence one loses to it.
effect_size_in_context: OPD at this scale buys +0.059 over the untrained student (0.6990 -> 0.7580). A budget-matched uniform random mask captures +0.035 of that; math_only captures all of it. So the regex recovers the ~41% of OPD's benefit that an uninformative selection leaves on the table, while capturing LESS teacher-student divergence than the random mask it beats.
caveat: The selection effect is learning-rate dependent -- measured directly, not inferred: +0.0243 (p=0.052) at 1e-5 and -0.0058 (p=0.173) at 3e-6, both matched-budget, 3 seeds each. The budget result is rate-robust; the selection result is not. random@0.20 and random@0.85 have 2 seeds, not 3.

lr_3e-6_control.finding: The matched-budget control re-run at 3e-6. The BUDGET effect replicates and stays zero (-0.0030, p=0.599, against -0.0027, p=0.722 at 1e-5). The SELECTION effect does NOT: +0.0243 at 1e-5 becomes -0.0058 at 3e-6. Selection matters only at the higher rate, where vanilla has degraded from 0.7580 to 0.7363; the mask recovers exactly that lost ground and no more. Every arm at either rate tops out at 0.758, so the mask repairs damage from an over-large learning rate rather than adding anything a well-tuned baseline lacks.

rkl_min_arm.definition: At each step, per rollout, keep the round(alpha*n) completion tokens with the SMALLEST per-token reverse KL -- KL(student||teacher), the trainer's own beta=1 loss. Budget-matched to v0 per batch. Implemented as top-k of the negated score.
rkl_min_arm.finding: Training on the tokens that contribute LEAST to the loss works. rkl_min captures 1.6% of the total divergence and trains at a loss of 0.0006 against vanilla's ~0.25 -- roughly 400x smaller -- and still edges out full-token OPD (+0.0065) and a budget-matched random draw (+0.0092). All three contrasts are null at 3 seeds; the point is that it works at all. Adam's update is invariant to a global rescaling of the loss, so the collapsed loss scale does not act as a reduced learning rate.
rkl_min_arm.breaks_the_linear_law: The 5-arm fit acc = 0.7742 - 0.0395*mass_per_token (r^2=0.93 over mass 0.55-1.77) predicts 0.7732 at mass 0.0248. Observed 0.7428, residual -0.0304 against +-0.007 for every other arm. Refitting with this point drops r^2 to 0.70. mass/token predicts well over its measured range and fails below it: there is an interior optimum near math_only's 0.55, not a monotone 'lower is better'.
